description: Frozen database baseline. Every value here is a claim the migration-replay job re-proves from an empty PostgreSQL 17 on every run. A value that changes legitimately must be raised in the SAME commit that changes the schema, so the diff shows both.

structuralTotalsEstablishedBy: PR CI run 19 (run id 30431556718), job `database-migration-replay / migration-replay`, artifact `evidence-migration-replay`, file `migration-replay.json`, at feature head 8d7bfff09cf914e00ff5ff4587341ece261185c3, started 2026-07-29T07:24:48Z, GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest, PostgreSQL 17 service container replayed from empty.
migrationCountNote: 119 through DBCR-P1-16-001. Raised to 120 by DBCR-P1-18-001 (20260731090000_rec_custody_release_visit_marker.sql), which closes P1-27-INT-013 — a Vehicle could be received exactly once, ever, because the terminal status `converted` sat inside the predicate of uq_reception_visits_open_vehicle.
forbiddenMigrationPrefixNote: This reserves a FILENAME series, not an ordinal. It forbids files literally beginning `120` — the `120_`/`120…_` shape a future phase would mint — and it is unrelated to a migration merely being the 120th in the tree. DBCR-P1-18-001 is the 120th migration and is named `20260731090000_…`, so it does not match and this pin stays exactly as it was. Do not 'reconcile' the two numbers: they measure different things, and weakening this to accommodate an ordinal would retire a real guard.
schemaHashNote: Produced by `npm run validate:schema-inventory -- --hash-only`, over the 17 RootLco business schemas only — which is why it reproduces on a developer's Supabase stack even though the structural totals below do not. Was a677eb05… from P1-18 through DBCR-P1-16-001. Raised here by DBCR-P1-18-001, which adds rec.reception_visits.custody_released_at, two rec functions and two triggers, and replaces uq_reception_visits_open_vehicle. The new value was measured locally BEFORE being copied from CI, and the two agreed digit for digit; a baseline raised from a CI log alone would only be recording that the log said something.
permissionCountNote: 100 through P1-21 and unchanged by P1-22, which declared only codes P1-11 had already seeded. P1-23 raises it to 104 by adding the four READ codes its operations declare: shared.notification.read, shared.notification.delivery.read, shared.document.archive and rpt.report.read. P1-15 seeded only the two shared WRITE capabilities because it delivered only writes; reading is a separate authority, and reusing the write codes would have meant anyone who may enqueue a notification may also read every recipient's inbox. Added to supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql, which is idempotent and additive — NOT a migration, so migrationCount stays 119 and schemaHash is unchanged. This pin did its job: all four codes were declared by routes and missing from the catalog, and every denial-based authorization test still passed, because a permission that does not exist cannot be held by anybody.
structuralTotalsDeltaNote: DBCR-P1-18-001 raised `functions` 514 -> 516 and `triggers` 541 -> 543; `tables`, `policies` and `security_definer` are untouched. The delta is +2 functions (rec.guard_custody_release_marker, rec.apply_custody_release) and +2 triggers (tg_reception_visits_custody_release_marker, tg_custody_history_apply_release), read off the migration rather than measured, BECAUSE these totals cannot be reproduced locally: they count every non-system schema, and a developer's Supabase stack carries auth/storage/realtime objects the CI plain-postgres container does not. Measured on the local stack the same queries return tables 292, functions 591, triggers 548 and security_definer 6 — none of which is comparable with the figures above. The schemaHash IS reproducible locally and was reproduced; these four are the ones CI alone can settle.
structuralTotalsNote: Recorded from the first GitHub-hosted run, using migration-replay-checks.mjs's OWN catalog queries. The earlier note warned that copying earlier phase-gate numbers across would compare two things that were never the same measurement, and run 19 proved that warning exact: `functions` here is 514, while scripts/db/schema-inventory.mjs reported 212 for the same database in the same run.
functionCountDiscrepancyNote: 516 and 214 are both correct; they count different populations, and the difference is entirely in the WHERE clause. migration-replay-checks.mjs counts `pg_proc` filtered only by `n.nspname NOT IN ('pg_catalog','information_schema')`, so it includes extension and public-namespace functions. schema-inventory.mjs counts `WHERE n.nspname = ANY($1)`, restricted to the 17 RootLco business schemas — and the per-schema breakdown in that same artifact sums to exactly 214 (org, iam, shared, crm, veh, apt, rec, wo, tech, dia, qms, svc, quo, inv, sal, wty, rpt). The 302-function difference is therefore extension-owned code, not RootLco code, and it is constant: the pair moved 514/212 -> 516/214 together when DBCR-P1-18-001 added two rec functions, which is what let 516 be derived rather than guessed. Neither figure was chosen for convenience: 516 belongs HERE because this file is enforced by the script that produces 516, and 214 remains the number to quote for RootLco's own schema and the one comparable with every prior phase gate. Do not 'reconcile' them by editing either.
structuralTotalsCrossChecks: tables 242, triggers 541 and policies 631 are identical under both scripts, and the hosted clean room independently reported 242 live tables, 999 indexes and 537 foreign keys. Only `functions` diverges.
seededStructuralTablesNote: Enumerated from an empty PostgreSQL 17 in run 19 after migrations and seeding, when iam.permissions held 100 rows (104 since P1-23; the row counts below are that run's record, not a pin): iam.permissions (100 rows), inv.units_of_measure (12), sal.payment_methods (3), wo.job_states (6), wo.job_transitions (10), wo.work_order_states (9), wo.work_order_transitions (15). Every one is a structural catalog — permissions, units, payment methods and the work-order state machine — and none is business data, so the no-fake-data policy holds: a freshly provisioned database still starts with no customers, vehicles, orders or invoices. Now that the list is recorded, migration-replay-checks.mjs FAILS on any populated business table outside it, which is the point of recording it. Row counts are deliberately not pinned; the check matches table names only, so seeding one more permission is not a build break.
seededStructuralTablesAsymmetryNote: The check flags UNEXPECTED populated tables, not missing ones. A seed that silently stops running therefore still passes this particular gate — it is caught elsewhere, by the smoke reads and by permissionCount (100 when this note was written, 104 since P1-23 — see permissionCountNote).
